stories.title: N-able Kills Legacy APIs, Patches 17 N-central Zero-Days
stories.summary: The patches target recently disclosed zero-days, as well as vulnerabilities already exploited in the wild.

stories.title: Uber notifies drivers of data breach affecting nearly 150,000 people
stories.summary: Ride-hailing company Uber is notifying nearly 150,000 drivers that attackers stole their data after breaching AI infrastructure provider Fireworks in early October.

stories.title: Access Dental Management Data Breach Impacts Over 340,000
stories.summary: Hackers breached Access Dental’s network and stole personal, health, and insurance information.

stories.title: Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
stories.summary: Ticket seller Fandango Media is notifying customers about a data breach that exposed payment card details entered on its checkout pages.

stories.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
stories.summary: Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, known as SHA pinning, has become the go-to defense against software supply chain attacks. Attackers have already found a way around it. stories.title: Optimizely hack infected CNN, Fox News, BBC, Salesforce sites with malware
stories.summary: A suspected supply chain attack targeting Optimizely has led to malicious JavaScript being loaded on numerous popular websites, including Zoom, CNN, Fox News, BBC, Salesforce, and GitLab, exposing visitors to scripts designed to steal cryptocurrency and payment information and exploit vulnerabilities in iOS devices.

stories.title: 7 Tips For Complying with CJIS Password and MFA Requirements
stories.summary: The FBI's latest CJIS Security Policy requires law enforcement agencies to strengthen password protections and enforce MFA across privileged and non-privileged accounts. Specops Software outlines seven practical steps to meet these requirements, block compromised passwords, and maintain compliance.

stories.title: New GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors Turn GitHub and SharePoint Into Covert C2 Channels
stories.summary: Government sectors in Asia and Africa have been targeted by an active cyber intrusion campaign that delivers to previously undocumented backdoors that leverage legitimate services like Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub for command‑and‑control (C2). The activity has been codenamed Operation ShadowCloud by Kaspersky. The Russian cybersecurity company said it identified the campaign in early 2026.
